findings.title: No-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not exist
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate now calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only method added on UsernamePasswordForm is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel). There is no no-arg overload and no static import, so this class does not compile. The re-authentication change that is supposed to keep the username form available when passkeys are enabled cannot build or run until the call matches a real method (for example isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), and only if that predicate does not itself require a non-null user).

findings.title: Passkey form data is only set up when a user is already known
findings.body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, and both authenticate() (around the fillContextForm call) and the error challenge() use that predicate as the only gate for webauthnAuth.fillContextForm. Previously the WebAuthn challenge, rpId, conditional-UI flag, and AUTH_CHALLENGE_NOTE were written when the user was not yet selected, which is the normal passkey/conditional-UI login. They are now written only during re-authentication, when context.getUser() is already set. A fresh login therefore renders without passkey data, so discoverable-credential login and the webauth form on the first page fail, and a failed unidentified login no longer restores that data on the error page. The user != null check should not be part of “passkeys enabled”; fillContextForm needs to run whenever passkeys are enabled, including when the user is still null.
